query: hyperscaler AI capex growth year over year
normalized: ai capex growth hyperscaler over year

output.content:
**Hyperscaler capex is accelerating sharply in 2026, with the “big four” (Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Meta) collectively indicating roughly **$730 billion** of annual spending at current guidance/run-rate levels; this is principally data-center, server, networking, and AI-compute infrastructure, though company definitions also include some non-AI investment. [[1, 2, 3, 4]]

| Hyperscaler | Latest 2026 capex indication | Reference prior-year capex | Implied YoY growth |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Amazon | ~$220bn cash capex | $131.8bn in FY2025 | **~67%** |
| Alphabet | $195–205bn; $200bn midpoint | $91.4bn normalized FY2025 capex | **~119%** at midpoint |
| Meta | $130–145bn; $137.5bn midpoint, including finance-lease principal | $69.7bn normalized FY2025 capex | **~97%** at midpoint |
| Microsoft | ~$175bn calendar-2026 reported capex expectation after lease-accounting change | FY2026 additions to P&E were $115.9bn, versus $64.6bn in FY2025 | **FY2026 actual growth: ~80%** |

Amazon raised its 2026 cash-capex estimate from about $200 billion to about $220 billion in July, while reported FY2025 capex was $131.819 billion, implying approximately **67%** growth using those measures. [[1, 5]] 

Alphabet lifted its 2026 capex range to **$195–205 billion** from **$180–190 billion**, citing faster capacity delivery to meet demand; against $91.447 billion of normalized FY2025 capex, the $200 billion midpoint implies approximately **119%** growth. [[2, 6]] 

Meta’s latest outlook is **$130–145 billion**, including principal payments on finance leases, versus $69.691 billion of normalized FY2025 capex; the $137.5 billion midpoint implies approximately **97%** growth, subject to the lease-inclusion definition difference. [[3, 7]] 

Microsoft’s directly reported fiscal-year capex proxy—additions to property and equipment—rose from **$64.551 billion in FY2025 to $115.948 billion in FY2026**, or approximately **80%** year over year. [[8]] 

Microsoft said its calendar-2026 capex investment expectation was about **$175 billion** after a lease-accounting change that shifts more future data-center leases from finance leases into operating leases; management explicitly said the change affects reported capex presentation rather than the underlying investment expectation. [[8, 4]]

**Takeaway:** On a like-for-like directional basis, 2026 hyperscaler AI-infrastructure capex is growing roughly **two-thirds to more than 100%** year over year for Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta, while Microsoft already delivered about **80%** growth in FY2026 reported additions to property and equipment. [[5, 2, 3, 8]] 

The aggregate should be treated as an indicative AI-infrastructure spending envelope rather than a fully standardized financial metric, because Amazon uses cash capex, Meta’s guidance includes finance-lease principal, Microsoft’s reported amount is affected by finance-versus-operating-lease classification, and Alphabet’s cited historical figure is normalized capex. [[5, 3, 4, 6]]
